overall_assessment: Strict local delta decision: not independently acceptable yet, due to the two medium missing regression proofs below; neither is evidence of a currently reproduced product bypass. This was a read-only evidence/source audit, not a new test, provider, device, or network execution. The cp22 index test is behaviorally useful: it calls the actual resolver, seeds 2,000 retired identities, ANALYZEs, and observes the named current_channel_id index without planner forcing; EPS-E2/A2 is acceptable as bounded local evidence, not an SLO. Retained FRC-E3/A1, BCI-E3/A1, and RLS-E1/A1 evidence remains proportionate: real BFF/PG barriers and readbacks, five-client scoped reads, and zero provider fan-out during listings. REG-SEC-01 is a real Nest/PostgreSQL signed-webhook journey with DI-bound provider doubles and effective foreign-global-first, session, credential, and outbound assertions. REG-SEC-11 exercises concurrent authenticated echoes inside the sender path and verifies one physical keyed message, trusted content/name, one send, no IN/unread/bot side effects, and one realtime publication. The two new browser journeys use real BFF session and PostgreSQL state; their provider/SDK controls remain bounded fixture seams. Their widened button locator does not weaken the contract because request operation, retained BU/channel/generation, fresh attempt/nonce/idempotency key, one channel, no duplicate BU, and unchanged ambiguous-exchange count are asserted. The expiry fixture is loopback-only, requires the disposable database family and fixture header, and updates only the exact NOVO/PENDING_AUTH attempt plus BU; the 32-hex attempt correction is aligned with source. Static named-path checks found no focused/skipped tests or fallback shortcut; structured evidence logging is not a behavioral bypass. Freshness/CI parity is supported by the retained cp24 pre-worker source/bundle attestation and complete 498-test raw, while cp25 is correctly limited to targeted wrapper/config and HTTPS/session evidence rather than credited with the earlier full run. Cutover inspection found current-identity, per-channel credential resolution across BFF/public/Typebot callers; no global-token fallback, legacy Evolution adoption, or query-time dual path. The narrowly approved official legacy-slot promotion remains constrained to the same BU/channel after provider proof and absent active credential; nullable legacy message records remain intact. D-01 through D-10 remain substantively adherent in this delta: ownership, SDK gating, CAS recovery, credential isolation, ambiguous-state handling, renewal/QR trust, identity/tombstone indexing, keyed ingress/callers, origin/session controls, and frozen provenance. The cp23 two-case 409 CHANNEL_SLOT_OCCUPIED result is genuine pre-product RED; earlier UUID/poll failures were harness-only, and accepted TQA-CP21-02 mixed/test-after provenance remains unchanged. VAL-05 remains mandatory and unwaived for overall completion, but is outside this strict local correction audit and is not re-raised as a local finding.
recommended_path: Do not accept the strict local delta gate until the two targeted negative regression proofs are added. First, make REG-SEC-10 observe the stale old-identity webhook's realtime side effect directly. Second, make NOVO recovery exercise an authoritative retained-slot mismatch and prove fail-safe behavior/no reservation. Re-run the affected PostgreSQL API and browser or focused component suites with the same freshness/source-hash discipline, then obtain a new independent delta disposition. No product redesign, new fixture escape hatch, global credential path, or broad re-audit is indicated. Preserve the accepted TQA-CP21-02 and dependency debt boundaries, and preserve VAL-05 as the separate mandatory external Meta/device/IN/OUT/recovery gate rather than treating it as local debt or rediscovering it through another whole audit.

findings.title: REG-SEC-10 does not directly prove that stale old-instance ingress emits no realtime event
findings.rationale: Source anchor: api-app/test/number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:707-711 submits old-instance stale content before the RealtimeService.publicarNaBu spy is installed at :732; the no-call assertion at :739 therefore covers only the later current-name PENDING_IDENTITY request. Why now: the approved REG-SEC-10 contract explicitly includes no stale content/unread/realtime/bot effect. Current source appears safe because evolution.controller.ts:31-37 returns when the retired identity has no current channel, so this is a missing regression proof rather than a demonstrated live defect. Blocking versus debt: it is a strict-local test-quality blocker because a required negative security behavior in the changed simulation is unobserved; it is not accepted process debt or the external VAL-05 gap.
findings.suggested_action: Install the realtime spy before the old-name stale messages.upsert request and assert its 200 acknowledgement produces zero realtime calls as well as zero message, conversation, unread, Typebot, and outbound effects. Retain the existing current-name pre-identity and verified-current same-key checks. A real observable realtime sink is an acceptable alternative to the spy; static early-return reasoning alone should not substitute for this regression assertion.

findings.title: Recovery tests cover only the matching retained-slot projection, not its required fail-safe mismatch path
findings.rationale: Source anchor: web-app/src/componentes/CadastroNumero.tsx:521-555 correctly checks captured attempt identity and exact channel/type/generation/currentAttemptId before reset, but web-app/e2e/number-onboarding.spec.ts:129-221 tests only matching expiry and ambiguous-exchange projections; the nearby lifecycle/component specs do not exercise novaTentativaMesmoBu mismatch rejection. Why now: D-03 and NUM-WEB-11 require recovery to avoid blind NOVO fallback or a stale retained-slot action. The positive browser assertions catch the old NOVO behavior but would still pass if a future change weakened the mismatch guards. Static source currently fails safe, so this is not an asserted product defect. Blocking versus debt: the changed recovery behavior lacks required negative regression evidence and is therefore a bounded local-gate blocker, not cosmetic test debt or a reassertion of VAL-05.
findings.suggested_action: Add a deterministic regression case where the refreshed authoritative BU projection has a missing or mismatched retained channel, generation, or currentAttemptId. Assert the safe error, no lifecycle reset that enables reservation, no POST to number-registrations, and no new channel or BU. A focused component test that controls the refresh result is sufficient; alternatively use a tightly scoped real-BFF/PostgreSQL fixture mutation. Keep the existing two real-browser happy recovery journeys unchanged.
